children.translated_text: <s>Daśarūpaka</s> (The Ten Forms of Drama)
Chapter 1
Salutations to that <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, whose throat swells like a lotus,
Resounding with the thunder of clouds of ichor, during the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance) of <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Śiva). // DhDaś 1.1 //
Those who delight in the imitation of the ten dramatic forms,

children.text: namaḥ sarvavide tasmai viṣṇave bharatāya ca // DhDaś_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Salutations to that all-knowing <s>Viṣṇu</s> and to <s>Bharata</s>. // DhDaś 1.2 //

children.text: kasyacideva kadācid dayayā viṣayaṃ sarasvatī viduṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s>, out of compassion, bestows her domain upon some learned person at some time;

children.text: ghaṭayati kamapi tamanyo jajati jano yena vaidagdhīm // DhDaś_1.3 //
children.translated_text: That person fashions something by which other people attain refinement. // DhDaś 1.3 //
Having extracted the essence from all the <s>Nigamas</s> (Vedas), <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā) created the <s>Nāṭyaveda</s> (Science of Drama);

children.text: cakre yasya prayogaṃ munirapi bharatastāṇḍavaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Bharata</s> put it into practice, and <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Śiva) performed the <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance);

children.text: śarvāṇī lāsyamasya pratipadamaparaṃ lakṣma kaḥ kartumīṣṭe
children.translated_text: <s>Śarvāṇī</s> (Pārvatī) performed the <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) — who else is capable of defining every aspect of it?

children.text: nāṭyānāṃ kintu kiñcit praguṇaracanayā lakṣaṇaṃ saṅkṣipāmi // DhDaś_1.4 //
children.translated_text: But I shall briefly summarize some characteristics of dramatic forms through a well-arranged composition. // DhDaś 1.4 //
When scattered about, confusion arises in the minds of the dull-witted;
Therefore, the meaning of that [Nāṭyaveda] is here condensed simply in its own words. // DhDaś 1.5 //
In dramatic compositions that overflow with bliss,
One of limited intellect sees mere erudition as their fruit;
Even the virtuous person who spoke of them as being like <s>itihāsa</s> (historical narrative) and the like —
Salutations to him who turned away from aesthetic delight. // DhDaś 1.6 //
<s>Nāṭya</s> (drama) is the imitation of conditions; it is called <s>rūpa</s> (visual form) because it is to be seen;

children.text: rūpakaṃ tat samāropād daśadhaiva rasāśrayam // DhDaś_1.7 //
children.translated_text: That <s>rūpaka</s> (dramatic composition), based on superimposition, is tenfold and has <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) as its basis. // DhDaś 1.7 //
<s>Nāṭaka</s> (heroic drama), <s>Prakaraṇa</s> (social drama), <s>Bhāṇa</s> (monologue), <s>Prahasana</s> (farce), <s>Ḍima</s> (spectacle play),

<s>Vyāyoga</s> (one-act military play), <s>Samavakāra</s> (multi-hero play), <s>Vīthī</s> (one-act sketch), <s>Aṅka</s> (lyrical play), and <s>Īhāmṛga</s> (hunt play) — thus [are the ten]. // DhDaś 1.8 //
Apart from these, <s>nṛtya</s> (expressive dance) is based on emotional states, and <s>nṛtta</s> (pure dance) is based on rhythm and tempo;

children.text: ādyaṃ padārthābhinayo mārgo deśo tathā param // DhDaś_1.9 //
children.translated_text: The first is the enactment of meaning through gestures; the latter pertains to regional style. // DhDaś 1.9 //
Each of these two is again twofold, distinguished as sweet and vigorous,
In the forms of <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) and <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance), they are auxiliaries to <s>nāṭaka</s> and other [dramatic forms]. // DhDaś 1.10 //

children.text: vastu netā rasasteṣāṃ bhedako vastu ca dvidhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vastu</s> (plot), <s>netā</s> (hero), and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) are the differentiators of those [dramatic forms]; and <s>vastu</s> is twofold:
The principal one is called <s>ādhikārika</s> (pertaining to the main subject), and the subsidiary is known as <s>prāsaṅgika</s> (incidental). // DhDaś 1.11 //
<s>Adhikāra</s> (principal interest) is the claim to the fruit; and the one who commands that [claim] is the principal [hero];
That which cannot be set aside and is all-pervading constitutes the <s>ādhikārika</s> (principal) plot. // DhDaś 1.12 //
The <s>prāsaṅgika</s> (incidental plot) is that whose own purpose serves the purpose of another, arising incidentally;

children.text: sānubandhaṃ patākākhyaṃ prakarī ca pradeśabhāk // DhDaś_1.13 //
children.translated_text: When it has a continuous connection, it is called <s>patākā</s> (episodic subplot); and <s>prakarī</s> (minor episode) partakes only of a portion. // DhDaś 1.13 //
The <s>prāsaṅgika</s> (incidental) is that whose own purpose serves the purpose of another, arising incidentally;
When it has a continuous connection, it is qualified by similarity of arrangement. // DhDaś 1.14 //
The [plot] is also threefold in three ways, by the distinction of being well-known, invented, or mixed:
The <s>prakhyāta</s> (well-known) is derived from <s>itihāsa</s> (historical narrative) and the like; the <s>utpādya</s> (invented) is the poet's creation;

children.text: miśraṃ ca saṅkarāt tābhyāṃ divyanartyādibhedataḥ // DhDaś_1.15 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>miśra</s> (mixed) arises from the combination of those two, with distinctions of divine, human, and other [characters]. // DhDaś 1.15 //
The <s>kārya</s> (object of attainment) consists of the three aims of life; it may be pure, or connected with one or many [subplots];
The <s>bīja</s> (seed) is its cause, briefly indicated yet expanded in many ways;
The <s>bindu</s> (drop) is the cause of resumption when there is an interruption in the subsidiary purpose. // DhDaś 1.16 //
The five <s>arthaprakṛtis</s> (source-elements of the plot), characterized as <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>bindu</s> (drop), <s>patākā</s> (episodic subplot),

children.text: arthaprakṛtayaḥ pañca tā etāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // DhDaś_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>prakarī</s> (minor episode), and <s>kārya</s> (object of attainment) — these have been declared. // DhDaś 1.17 //
There are five <s>avasthās</s> (stages of action) of the <s>kārya</s> (object) when it is undertaken by those who seek the fruit:
<s>Ārambha</s> (beginning), <s>yatna</s> (effort), <s>prāptyāśā</s> (hope of attainment), <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment), and <s>phalāgama</s> (attainment of the fruit). // DhDaś 1.18 //
<s>Ārambha</s> (beginning) is mere eagerness for obtaining the greater fruit;
<s>Prayatna</s> (effort) is exertion accompanied by great haste when that [fruit] is not obtained. // DhDaś 1.19 //
<s>Prāptyāśā</s> (hope of attainment) is the possibility of obtaining [the fruit] through [alternating] hopes of success and fears of failure;
<s>Niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment) is the firm certainty of obtaining [the fruit] from the absence of obstacles;
<s>Phalayoga</s> (attainment of the fruit) is the complete realization of the entire fruit, as stated. // DhDaś 1.20 //
The five <s>arthaprakṛtis</s> (source-elements), conjoined with the five <s>avasthās</s> (stages of action),

children.text: yathāsaṅkhyena jāyante mukhādyāḥ pañca sandhayaḥ // DhDaś_1.21 //
children.translated_text: Give rise, in corresponding order, to the five <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) beginning with <s>mukha</s> (opening). // DhDaś 1.21 //
A <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) is the internal connection of a single purpose, when there is continuity of the [same] strand;
<s>Mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>avamarśa</s> (pause of deliberation), and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> (conclusion). // DhDaś 1.22 //
<s>Mukha</s> (opening) is the origination of the <s>bīja</s> (seed), giving rise to various purposes and <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments);
Its <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs) are twelve, following the connection of <s>bīja</s> (seed) and <s>ārambha</s> (beginning). // DhDaś 1.23 //
<s>Upakṣepa</s> (introduction), <s>parikara</s> (preparation), <s>parinyāsa</s> (elaboration), <s>vilobhana</s> (allurement),
<s>Yukti</s> (reasoning), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (nurturing),
<s>Udbheda</s> (disclosure), <s>bheda</s> (splitting), and <s>karaṇa</s> (effecting) — these are self-explanatory; now their definitions: // DhDaś 1.24 //
<s>Upakṣepa</s> (introduction) is the planting of the <s>bīja</s> (seed); <s>parikriyā</s> (preparation) is its expansion;
<s>Parinyāsa</s> (elaboration) is its completion; <s>vilobhana</s> (allurement) arises from the narration of merits. // DhDaś 1.25 //
<s>Yukti</s> (reasoning) is the deliberation over purposes; <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) is the arrival of happiness;
<s>Samādhāna</s> (resolution) is the arrival of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) [at fruition]; <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement) is what produces joy or sorrow. // DhDaś 1.26 //
<s>Paribhāva</s> (nurturing) is a state of inspired wonder; <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure) is the revealing of what is hidden;

children.text: karaṇaṃ prakṛtārambho bhedaḥ protsāhanā matā // DhDaś_1.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karaṇa</s> (effecting) is the commencement of the principal [action]; <s>bheda</s> (splitting) is considered to be encouragement. // DhDaś 1.27 //
Like something seen and yet unseen, the <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure) [of the seed] constitutes the <s>pratimukha</s> (progression);
Its <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs) are thirteen, following the connection of <s>bindu</s> (drop) and <s>prayatna</s> (effort). // DhDaś 1.28 //
<s>Vilāsa</s> (dalliance), <s>parisarpa</s> (pursuit), <s>vidhūta</s> (disturbance), <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>narma</s> (jest),
<s>Narmadyuti</s> (jest-splendor), <s>pragayaṇa</s> (counter-speech), <s>nirodha</s> (restraint), <s>paryupāsana</s> (supplication),
<s>Vajra</s> (thunderbolt), <s>puṣpa</s> (flower), <s>upanyāsa</s> (persuasion), <s>varṇasaṃhāra</s> (bringing together of parties) — thus also.
<s>Vilāsa</s> (dalliance) is desire and longing for objects; <s>parisarpa</s> is the tracing of what is seen and then lost;
<s>Vidhūta</s> (disturbance) is disaffection; <s>śama</s> (tranquility) is its calming. // DhDaś 1.30 //
<s>Narma</s> (jest) contains humor; <s>dyuti</s> (splendor) is the firmness born of it;

children.text: uttarā vāk pragayaṇaṃ hitarodho nirodhanam // DhDaś_1.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pragayaṇa</s> (counter-speech) is a reply; <s>nirodha</s> (restraint) is the obstruction of what is beneficial. // DhDaś 1.31 //
<s>Paryupāsana</s> (supplication) is entreaty; <s>puṣpa</s> (flower) is a speech with distinction;
<s>Upanyāsa</s> (persuasion) is speech with stratagem; <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) is directly harsh speech;
<s>Varṇasaṃhāra</s> (bringing together of parties) is the assembling of the four classes [of characters]. // DhDaś 1.32 //
<s>Garbha</s> (development) is the repeated searching for the <s>bīja</s> (seed) that has been seen and lost;

children.text: dvādaśāṅgaḥ patākā syān na vā syāt prāptisambhavaḥ // DhDaś_1.33 //
children.translated_text: It has twelve <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs); the <s>patākā</s> (episodic subplot) may or may not be present; there is the possibility of attainment. // DhDaś 1.33 //
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication), <s>mārga</s> (path), <s>rūpa</s> (semblance), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration), <s>krama</s> (sequence),
<s>Saṅgraha</s> (conciliation), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>toṭaka</s> (agitation), and <s>adhivala</s> (persistence) — likewise,
<s>Udvega</s> (anxiety), <s>sambhrama</s> (confusion), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), and the definition is given:
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabrication) is deception; <s>mārga</s> (path) is the declaration of the true state of affairs. // DhDaś 1.35 //
<s>Rūpa</s> (semblance) is a speech resembling conjecture; <s>udāhṛti</s> (illustration) is speech with praise;
<s>Krama</s> (sequence) is the attainment of what has been deliberated upon; others [call it] knowledge of states of being. // DhDaś 1.36 //
<s>Saṅgraha</s> (conciliation) is speech of diplomacy and generosity; <s>abhyūha</s> (inference) is reasoning from signs;
<s>Adhivala</s> (persistence) is conspiracy; <s>toṭaka</s> (agitation) is angry speech. // DhDaś 1.37 //
<s>Udvega</s> (anxiety) is fear of the enemy; <s>sambhrama</s> (confusion) is alarm and fright;
<s>Ākṣepa</s> (objection) is declared to arise from the sprouting of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) from the <s>garbha</s> (development). // DhDaś 1.38 //
Where one deliberates in anger, or where [deliberation arises] from calamity or from enticement —

That is <s>avamarśa</s> (pause of deliberation), whose purpose is the <s>bīja</s> (seed) split open from the <s>garbha</s> (development); [here follows] the collection of its <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs). // DhDaś 1.39 //
Therein are <s>apavāda</s> (censure), <s>sampheṭa</s> (quarrel), <s>vidrava</s> (flight), <s>drava</s> (rout), <s>śakti</s> (power),
<s>Dyuti</s> (determination), <s>prasaṅga</s> (involvement), <s>chalana</s> (deception), <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve), <s>virodhana</s> (opposition),
<s>Prayocanā</s> (instigation), <s>vicalana</s> (wavering), and <s>ādāna</s> (seizure) — thirteen [in all]. // DhDaś 1.40 //
<s>Apavāda</s> (censure) is the proclamation of faults; <s>sampheṭa</s> (quarrel) is angry speech;
<s>Vidrava</s> (flight) is killing, imprisonment, and the like; <s>drava</s> (rout) is the humiliation of an elder. // DhDaś 1.41 //
<s>Śakti</s> (power) is the pacification of hostility; <s>dyuti</s> (determination) is threatening and causing distress;
<s>Prasaṅga</s> (involvement) is the praise of elders; <s>chalana</s> (deception) is disrespect. // DhDaś 1.42 //
<s>Vyavasāya</s> (resolve) is the declaration of one's own strength; <s>virodhana</s> (opposition) is the resistance of the enraged;
<s>Prayocanā</s> (instigation) is the display of future [consequences] through the counsel of the accomplished;
<s>Vicalana</s> (wavering) is boasting; <s>ādāna</s> (seizure) is the gathering up of the action. // DhDaś 1.43 //
Where the purposes of the opening and other [junctures], which contain the <s>bīja</s> (seed) and are scattered about,

children.text: aikārthyamupanīyante yatra nirvahaṇaṃ hi tat // DhDaś_1.44 //
children.translated_text: Are brought together to a single conclusion — that is <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (denouement). // DhDaś 1.44 //
<s>Sandhi</s> (reconciliation), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>grathana</s> (weaving), <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (dialogue),
<s>Prasāda</s> (grace), <s>ānanda</s> (joy), <s>samaya</s> (agreement), <s>kṛti</s> (accomplishment), <s>bhāṣā</s> (speech), <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace),
<s>Pūrvabhāva</s> (prior state), <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion), and <s>praśasti</s> (benediction) — fourteen [in all]. // DhDaś 1.45 //
<s>Sandhi</s> (reconciliation) is the approaching of the <s>bīja</s> (seed); <s>vibodha</s> (awakening) is the search for the purpose;
<s>Grathana</s> (weaving) is the gathering up of that; <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination) is the narration of what has been experienced. // DhDaś 1.46 //
<s>Paribhāṣā</s> (dialogue) is mutual conversation; <s>prasāda</s> (grace) is supplication;
<s>Ānanda</s> (joy) is the attainment of what was desired; <s>samaya</s> (agreement) is the departure of sorrow. // DhDaś 1.47 //
<s>Kṛti</s> (accomplishment) is the calming after attaining the object; <s>bhāṣaṇa</s> (speech) is the attainment of honor and the like;
<s>Pūrvabhāva</s> (prior state) and <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace) are the marvelous attainment upon viewing the accomplished purpose;
<s>Upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion) is the obtaining of boons and the winding up of the poem; <s>praśasti</s> (benediction) is the utterance of blessings. // DhDaś 1.48 //
The arrangement of the desired purpose, the concealment of what should be hidden, the revelation [of what should be known],
The attachment [of the audience], the wonder of the performance, and the non-diminishing of the narrative —
A twofold division should be made for the removal of all subject matter:
Some things should be merely indicated, while others should be presented as visible or audible. // DhDaś 1.50 //
What is tasteless and unfitting there — the expansion of the plot — should be indicated [off-stage];
but what is to be shown [on-stage] should be uninterruptedly imbued with the sweet and exalted <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments). (DhDaś 1.51)
What is to be indicated should be conveyed through five devices that introduce the subject-matter:
<s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude), <s>cūlikā</s> (poetic tag), <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face), <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-transition), and <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene). (DhDaś 1.52)
The <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude) is a summary indicator of past and future
portions of the story, employed by middle-rank characters;
when performed by one or more, it is 'pure' (<s>śuddha</s>); 'mixed' (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) when by low and middle [characters]. (DhDaś 1.53)
Similar to that, but with non-exalted speech, employed by low-rank characters,
the <s>praveśaka</s> (introductory scene) is within [the interval of] two acts, an indicator of the remaining subject-matter. (DhDaś 1.54)
The indication of the subject of the <s>cūlikā</s> (poetic tag) is by those positioned behind the curtain;
the <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face) is by characters at the end of an act, through the indication of the subject of a broken [i.e., interrupted] act. (DhDaś 1.55)
The <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-transition) is the fall of an act at its end without a break [in action];

children.text: ebhiḥ saṃsūcayet sūcyaṃ dṛśyamaṅkaiḥ pradarśayet // DhDaś_1.56 //
children.translated_text: by these [five], one should indicate what is to be indicated; what is to be shown should be displayed through acts. (DhDaś 1.56)
Considering the conventions of drama, the subject-matter is again desired as threefold:
for all [characters], what is necessarily heard (<s>śrāvya</s>) and what is not to be heard (<s>aśrāvya</s>). (DhDaś 1.57)
What is heard by all is <s>prakāśa</s> (open speech); what is not to be heard is considered <s>svagata</s> (aside);
the other, twofold, is called the dramatic convention: <s>janānta</s> (aside to a person) and <s>apavārita</s> (concealed speech). (DhDaś 1.58)
By warding off others with the <s>tripatāka</s> hand-gesture, the conversation that takes place

children.text: anyonyāmantraṇaṃ yat syāj janānte taj janāntikam /
children.translated_text: between two people aside is <s>janāntika</s> (aside to a person);
a secret spoken to another by turning away is <s>apavārita</s> (concealed speech). (DhDaś 1.59)

children.text: kiṃ bravīṣyevamityādi vinā pātraṃ bravīti yat /
children.translated_text: 'What shall I say?' and such — what [a character] speaks without [addressing] another character,
and what, though not [actually] heard, one responds to as if having heard — that is called <s>ākāśabhāṣita</s> (speech into the void). (DhDaś 1.60)
Having thus considered the entire range of subject-matter distinctions,
and having studied the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> and other [epics] as well as the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s> (Great Story),
one should then compose, in accordance with the <s>rasas</s> suited to the hero,
a variegated story with appropriate and beautiful verbal elaborations. (DhDaś 1.61)
Chapter 2
The <s>netā</s> (hero) is refined, sweet-natured, generous, skillful, pleasing in speech,

children.text: raktalokaḥ śucirvāṅmī rūḍhavaṃśaḥ sthiro yuvā // DhDaś_2.1 //
children.translated_text: beloved of the people, pure, eloquent, of established lineage, steadfast, and youthful. (DhDaś 2.1)
Endowed with intelligence, enthusiasm, memory, wisdom, arts, and pride,
brave, firm, resplendent, learned in the <s>śāstras</s> (sciences), and righteous —
he is fourfold in kind: <s>dhīralalita</s> (calm-graceful), <s>dhīraśānta</s> (calm-tranquil), <s>dhīrodātta</s> (calm-exalted), and <s>dhīroddhata</s> (calm-vehement). (DhDaś 2.2)
The <s>dhīralalita</s> (calm-graceful) is carefree, devoted to the arts, happy, and soft;
the <s>dhīraśānta</s> (calm-tranquil) possesses the common qualities and is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or the like. (DhDaś 2.3)
Of great spirit, extremely profound, patient, not boastful,
steadfast, with concealed pride — the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (calm-exalted) is firm in his vows. (DhDaś 2.4)
Predominantly proud and jealous, devoted to deceit and trickery,
the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (calm-vehement) is egotistic, fickle, fierce, and boastful. (DhDaś 2.5)

children.text: sa dakṣiṇaḥ śaṭho dhṛṣṭaḥ pūrvāṃ pratyanyayā hṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (gallant), <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful), or <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold): when won over from a former [beloved] by another,
he is <s>dakṣiṇa</s> if tender-hearted toward the [former] one; <s>śaṭha</s> if he secretly acts displeasingly;
<s>dhṛṣṭa</s> if he openly shows his altered state; and <s>anukūla</s> (faithful) if devoted to one <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) alone. (DhDaś 2.6)
The <s>patākānāyaka</s> (subsidiary hero) is another; the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> is a discerning [companion];
his attendant is devoted and slightly inferior to him in qualities. (DhDaś 2.7)
The <s>viṭa</s> (libertine) is another, learned in one art; and the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) is a maker of laughter;

children.text: lubdho dhīroddhatastabdhaḥ(?) pāpakṛd vyasanī ripuḥ // DhDaś_2.8 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ripu</s> (enemy) is greedy, of the calm-vehement type, obstinate, evil-doing, and addicted to vices. (DhDaś 2.8)
<s>Śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (depth), <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness), <s>tejas</s> (brilliance),
<s>lalita</s> (gracefulness), and <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity) — these eight are the innate manly qualities. (DhDaś 2.9)
<s>Śobhā</s> (splendor) is: contempt toward the low, rivalry toward the superior, and skill in valor;

children.text: gatiḥ sadhairyā dṛṣṭiśca vilāse sammitaṃ vacaḥ // DhDaś_2.10 //
children.translated_text: bearing with steadfastness and a [commanding] gaze; <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry) is measured speech. (DhDaś 2.10)
A smooth alteration [of expression] is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness); <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (depth) is that
by whose power no alteration is perceived even in the greatest agitation. (DhDaś 2.11)
Not wavering from one's resolve even amid a host of obstacles is <s>sthairya</s> (firmness);
not tolerating insult even at the cost of one's life is <s>tejas</s> (brilliance). (DhDaś 2.12)
<s>Lalita</s> (gracefulness) is the natural, soft bearing of the body in the manner of erotic gestures;
<s>audārya</s> (magnanimity) is giving away even one's life upon a pleasing word, with generous support. (DhDaś 2.13)
The <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) is threefold: <s>svā</s> (one's own wife), <s>anyā</s> (another's wife), and <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (a courtesan);

children.text: mugdhā madhyā pragalbheti svīyā śīlārjavādiyuk // DhDaś_2.14 //
children.translated_text: the <s>svīyā</s> (one's own) is endowed with virtue, sincerity, etc., and is <s>mugdhā</s> (naive), <s>madhyā</s> (moderate), or <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold). (DhDaś 2.14)

children.text: mugdhā navavayaḥkāmā ratau vāmā mṛduḥ krudhi /
children.translated_text: The <s>mugdhā</s> (naive heroine) is of fresh youth and desire, contrary in love, and soft in anger;
the <s>madhyā</s> (moderate) is of budding youth and dawning passion, capable of love-making in the intervals of modesty. (DhDaś 2.15)
The <s>dhīrā</s> (steadfast) [heroine] would grieve her beloved by anger with a smile and crooked speech; the <s>madhyā</s> (moderate) with tears when he comes after being with another;
the <s>adhīrā</s> (unsteady) with harsh words. (DhDaś 2.16)
Blinded by youth, maddened by passion, the <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold heroine) — even as her beloved's body
is dissolving [in her embrace] — from sheer bliss becomes unconscious even at the commencement of love-making. (DhDaś 2.17)
The <s>dhīrā</s> (steadfast) [type of the bold] sits dissembling in anger, shedding tears in lovemaking; the <s>adhīrā</s> (unsteady) would

children.text: santarjya tāḍayen madhyā madhyādhīreva taṃ vadet /
children.translated_text: threaten and strike; the <s>madhyādhīrā</s> (moderate-unsteady) would speak [reproachfully] to him;

children.text: dvedhā jyeṣṭhā kaniṣṭā cetyamugdhā dvādaśoditāḥ // DhDaś_2.18 //
children.translated_text: these [heroines] not naive are twofold — elder and younger — thus twelve non-naive [types] are described. (DhDaś 2.18)
The <s>anyā</s> (another's woman) is a maiden or a married woman; the unmarried one's role is not in <s>Aṅgirasa</s> [i.e., not the primary subject];
a maiden should create the connection of subsidiary and principal [plots] according to the desire of love. (DhDaś 2.19)
The <s>sādhāraṇastrī</s> (courtesan) is a <s>gaṇikā</s>, endowed with proficiency in arts, boldness, and cunning;
she [serves] those whose hidden desires for pleasure are unknown — the independent, the self-important, and the impotent. (DhDaś 2.20)
As if enamored, she should delight the wealthy; the penniless she should merely dismiss;
but when truly in love, she does not act [calculatingly] — this [type] does not occur in divine or royal settings. (DhDaś 2.21)
For these [heroines] there are eight states, beginning with <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> (she whose lord is under her control);
she whose lover is near and devoted, who is happy — that is the <s>svādhīnabhartṛkā</s>. (DhDaś 2.22)
With joy, the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (one dressed for the tryst) adorns herself when her beloved is about to come;
when he delays without deception, she becomes the <s>virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> (one pining in separation), anxious-minded. (DhDaś 2.23)
When his attachment to another is known and revealed, she is the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (one betrayed), stained with jealousy;
the <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (one separated by a quarrel), when the quarrel is over, is afflicted with remorse and pain. (DhDaś 2.24)
The <s>vipralabdhā</s> (one deceived) is extremely humiliated when the appointed time passes without his arrival;
the <s>proṣitapriyā</s> (one whose beloved is abroad) is she whose beloved has gone to a distant land on business;
the <s>abhisārikā</s> (one who goes to meet her lover) is desire-afflicted and goes to meet or sends for her beloved. (DhDaś 2.25)
The last six [states] are accompanied by anxiety, sighing, weariness, tears, pallor, languor, and lack of adornment;

children.text: yuktāḥ ṣaḍantyā dve cādye kroḍaujjvalyapraharṣitaiḥ // DhDaś_2.26 //
children.translated_text: the first two [states] are accompanied by embrace, radiance, and delight. (DhDaś 2.26)
The messengers (<s>dūtī</s>) are: a maidservant, a female friend, a craftswoman, a foster-sister, a neighbor,

children.text: liṅginī śilpinī svaṃ ca netṛmitraguṇānvitāḥ // DhDaś_2.27 //
children.translated_text: a female ascetic, an artisan-woman, and oneself — [all] endowed with the qualities of the hero's friend. (DhDaś 2.27)
In youth, the innate ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) of women are twenty;

children.text: bhāvo hāvaśca helā ca trayastatra śarīrajāḥ // DhDaś_2.28 //
children.translated_text: <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), <s>hāva</s> (amorous gesture), and <s>helā</s> (dalliance) — these three arise from the body. (DhDaś 2.28)

children.text: śobhā kāntiśca dīptiśca mādhuryaṃ ca pragalbhatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>kānti</s> (radiance), <s>dīpti</s> (lustre), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), and <s>pragalbhatā</s> (boldness),

children.text: audāryaṃ dhairyamityete sapta bhāvā ayatnajāḥ // DhDaś_2.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity), and <s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness) — these seven <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) arise effortlessly. (DhDaś 2.29)
<s>Līlā</s> (playfulness), <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry), <s>vicchitti</s> (charm), <s>vibhrama</s> (confusion), <s>kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotion),
<s>moṭṭāyita</s> (pouting), <s>kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned anger), <s>bibboka</s> (disdain), <s>lalita</s> (grace), and

children.text: vihṛtaṃ ceti vijñeyā daśa bhāvāḥ svabhāvajāḥ // DhDaś_2.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>vihṛta</s> (bashful concealment) — these ten <s>bhāvas</s> should be known as arising from one's own nature. (DhDaś 2.30)
From innate <s>sattva</s> (temperament) that is without alteration, <s>bhāva</s> is the first modification;
the emergence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) is <s>hāva</s>, produced through alterations of eyes and brows. (DhDaś 2.31)
That very [hāva], when it is a clearly manifest indicator of <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment), is <s>helā</s> (dalliance);
<s>śobhā</s> (splendor) is the adornment of the limbs through beauty, enjoyment, and youth. (DhDaś 2.32)
That very [śobhā], when a shadow is cast by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), is remembered as <s>kānti</s> (radiance);

children.text: anulabaṇatvaṃ mādhuryaṃ dīptiḥ kāntestu vistaraḥ // DhDaś_2.33 //
children.translated_text: gracefulness is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness); <s>dīpti</s> (lustre) is the expansion of <s>kānti</s>. (DhDaś 2.33)
Fearlessness is <s>prāgalbhya</s> (boldness); <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity) is constant modesty;
<s>dhairya</s> (steadfastness) is not being disturbed by fickleness; it is a mental disposition, without boasting. (DhDaś 2.34)
<s>Līlā</s> (playfulness) is the imitation of the beloved through sweet bodily gestures;
<s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry) is a momentary distinction in bodily movements and such. (DhDaś 2.35)
Even a slight arrangement of adornment that enhances beauty is <s>vicchitti</s> (charm);
<s>vibhrama</s> (confusion) is the hasty misplacement of ornaments at the wrong positions. (DhDaś 2.36)
<s>Kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotion) is the mingling of anger, tears, joy, fear, and so forth;
<s>moṭṭāyita</s> (pouting) is [the expression] in the contemplation of the beloved's states, desired conversations, and such. (DhDaś 2.37)
<s>Kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned anger) is being inwardly delighted yet showing anger at the seizing of hair or lip;
<s>bibboka</s> (disdain) is an act of indifference even when pride or self-regard is addressed. (DhDaś 2.38)
A delicate, smooth arrangement of the limbs is <s>lalita</s> (grace);

children.text: prāptakālaṃ na yad brūyād vrīḍayā vihṛtaṃ hi tat // DhDaś_2.39 //
children.translated_text: not saying what is appropriate at the time due to bashfulness is <s>vihṛta</s> (bashful concealment). (DhDaś 2.39)

children.text: mantrī svaṃ vobhayaṃ vāpi sakhā tasyārthacintane /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s> (minister) may be his own, or both [his own and the hero's]; the <s>sakhā</s> (friend) assists in deliberating on affairs;
by the minister, the <s>lalita</s> (graceful hero) [succeeds]; the rest have their success dependent on the minister. (DhDaś 2.40)
The <s>ṛtvik</s> (ritual priest) and <s>purohita</s> (court priest) [serve] in matters of <s>dharma</s>; ascetics and <s>Vedic</s> scholars [likewise];
the <s>suhṛt</s> (well-wisher), the <s>kumāra</s> (prince), and the forest-dweller [serve] in matters of punishment; feudatories and soldiers [likewise]. (DhDaś 2.41)
In the inner quarters: <s>varṣavaras</s> (eunuchs), <s>kirātas</s> (tribals), mutes, and dwarfs.
<s>Mlecchas</s>, <s>Ābhīras</s>, <s>Śakāras</s>, and others are employed according to their respective functions. (DhDaś 2.42)
All [characters] have a threefold [classification] as superior, middling, and inferior.
From the gradation of the qualities mentioned, [they are further divided as] best, etc.

children.text: evaṃ nāṭye vidhātavyo nāyakaḥ saparicchadaḥ // DhDaś_2.43 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in a drama, the hero is to be fashioned along with his retinue. (DhDaś 2.43)
The <s>vṛtti</s> (dramatic style), whose essence is his [the hero's] activity, is fourfold. Among them, <s>Kaiśikī</s> (the graceful style)
[consists of] soft movements — gait, dance, coquetry, and the like — [and] amorous gestures of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) [sentiment].
It has four limbs: <s>narman</s> (wit), <s>narmasphiñja</s>, <s>narmasphoṭa</s>, and <s>narmagarbha</s>. (DhDaś 2.44)
<s>Narman</s> (wit) is clever play, whose essence is pleasing the beloved,
produced in three ways: with humor alone, with humor combined with the erotic, and with humor combined with fear. (DhDaś 2.45)
With the erotic, it is also threefold — through self-introduction, through enjoyment, and through pride.
The pure [variety] is twofold; that with fear is also twofold — through speech, dress, and gesture.
All [varieties] are accompanied by humor — thus <s>narman</s> is declared to be of eighteen kinds. (DhDaś 2.46)
<s>Narmasphiñja</s> has a pleasant beginning and an ending with fear, in a new encounter.
<s>Narmasphoṭa</s>, however, hints at emotions with small bits [of dialogue], having little <s>rasa</s>. (DhDaś 2.47)
<s>Narmagarbha</s> is a concealed counter-stratagem for a purpose,
with limbs both humorous and non-humorous — by these, this is the <s>Kaiśikī</s> [style]. (DhDaś 2.48)
The <s>Sāttvatī</s> (the grand style) is free from sorrow, [characterized by] fortitude (<s>sattva</s>), heroism, renunciation, compassion, and swiftness.
Its [limbs are]: <s>saṃlāpaka</s>, <s>utthāpaka</s>, <s>sāṅghātya</s>, and <s>parivartaka</s>. (DhDaś 2.49)
<s>Saṃlāpaka</s> is deep speech, containing various emotions and <s>rasas</s>, [exchanged] mutually.
<s>Utthāpaka</s>, however, is where at the outset one incites another to battle. (DhDaś 2.50)
<s>Sāṅghātya</s> is the breaking of an alliance through stratagem, purpose, fate, or power.
<s>Parivartaka</s> is the non-performance of actions [already] begun for the purpose of a rising [action]. (DhDaś 2.51)
By these four limbs, this <s>Sāttvatī</s> [is constituted]. The <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> (the violent style), again,
[consists of] gestures of magic, conjuring, battle, fury, frenzy, and the like.
It has [four limbs]: <s>saṅkṣiptikā</s>, <s>sampheṭa</s>, <s>vastūtthāna</s>, and <s>avapātana</s>. (DhDaś 2.52)
<s>Saṅkṣiptikā</s> (condensation) is a condensed arrangement of the plot through the employment of artifice.
By the withdrawal of the former leader, [and] the assumption of another leader. (DhDaś 2.53)
<s>Sampheṭa</s> (clash) is a violent encounter between two who are enraged and excited.
<s>Vastūtthāpana</s> (conjuring up a thing) is an object conjured up by magic and the like.
<s>Avapātana</s> (sudden fall) [is characterized by] exits, entrances, fright, and flight. (DhDaś 2.54)
By these four limbs, this [<s>Ārabhaṭī</s> is constituted]. There is no <s>Arthavṛtti</s> (material style) beyond these.

children.text: caturthī bhāratī sāpi vācyā nāṭakalakṣaṇe // DhDaś_2.55 //
children.translated_text: The fourth, <s>Bhāratī</s> (the verbal style), will also be described in the definition of <s>Nāṭaka</s>. (DhDaś 2.55)
Those who read <s>Kaiśikī</s>, <s>Sāttvatī</s>, <s>Arthavṛtti</s>, and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> —
the followers of <s>Udbhaṭa</s> assert a fifth <s>vṛtti</s> [as well]. (DhDaś 2.56)
<s>Kaiśikī</s> [is employed] in the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) [sentiment]; <s>Sāttvatī</s> in the heroic (<s>vīra</s>); <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> again

children.text: rase raudre ca bībhatse vṛttiḥ sarvatra bhāratī // DhDaś_2.57 //
children.translated_text: in the furious (<s>raudra</s>) and the disgusting (<s>bībhatsa</s>) sentiments; <s>Bhāratī</s> [is employed] everywhere. (DhDaś 2.57)
The <s>pravṛttis</s> (local usages) are characterized by region, language, actions, and dress.
These are derived from the world and from the gods; one should employ them as appropriate. (DhDaś 2.58)
For men who are not low-born and who are cultured, Sanskrit is [the language] for verse [and prose].
Also for female ascetics, the chief queen, [and] sometimes for ministers' wives and courtesans. (DhDaś 2.59)

children.text: strīṇāṃ tu prākṛtaṃ prāyaḥ śūrasenyadhameṣu ca /
children.translated_text: For women generally, <s>Prākṛt</s> [is used]; also for <s>Śūrasena</s> [characters] and low [characters].
For <s>Piśācas</s> and the extremely low, <s>Paiśāca</s> [is used]; likewise <s>Māgadhī</s>. (DhDaś 2.60)

children.text: yaddeśaṃ nīcapātraṃ yat taddeśaṃ tasya bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the region of a low character — the speech of that [character] is of that region.
But when there is a reason, even for superior characters and others, a transgression of language [norms] should be made. (DhDaś 2.61)
'<s>Bhagavan</s>' (Blessed one) — with [honorific] endings — is [used to address] the learned, gods, sages, and ascetics.
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, ministers, and elder brothers [are addressed as] '<s>Ārya</s>'; the stage-manager (<s>naṭī</s>) and <s>sūtradhāra</s> [address each other as] '<s>Mṛta</s>.' (DhDaś 2.62)

A charioteer [addresses a warrior] as '<s>Āyuṣman</s>' (long-lived one). [Teachers address] pupils, sons, and younger brothers of venerable persons [as] '<s>Vatsa</s>' (dear child); [and they address] the father [as] '<s>Tāta</s>';

children.text: vatseti tātaḥ pūjyo'pi sugṛhītābhidhastu taiḥ // DhDaś_2.63 //
children.translated_text: a venerable person [is addressed] by them with his well-known name. (DhDaś 2.63)

children.text: bhāvo'nugena sūtrī ca mārṣetyetena so'pi ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> [addresses] a colleague as '<s>Bhāva</s>'; and '<s>Mārṣa</s>' — by this, he [addresses] him as well.
'<s>Deva</s>' (Lord) and '<s>Svāmin</s>' — [are used to address] the king by servants; '<s>Bhaṭṭa</s>' — by the lowest [servants]. (DhDaś 2.64)
Women are to be addressed like [one's] wife — by superior, middling, and inferior [characters respectively].

children.text: samā haleti praṣyā ca hañje veśyājjukā tathā // DhDaś_2.65 //
children.translated_text: An equal [female is addressed as] '<s>Hale</s>'; a maidservant as '<s>Hañje</s>'; a courtesan and female jester likewise. (DhDaś 2.65)
A procuress [is addressed as] '<s>Ambe</s>' (mother) by followers, or [as one would address] a venerable elderly woman.

children.text: vidūṣakeṇa bhavatī rājñī ceṭīti śabdyate // DhDaś_2.66 //
children.translated_text: By the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester), [the queen is addressed as] '<s>Bhavatī</s>'; the queen [addresses] a maidservant as '<s>Ce���ī</s>.' (DhDaś 2.66)
The gestures, qualities, illustrations, temperaments, and emotional states [of characters] —
undivided into the ten conditions of the hero, [described] in their entirety —

children.text: ko vaktumīśo bharato na yo vā
children.translated_text: who is able to declare [them all]? Not one who is not <s>Bharata</s> [himself],

children.text: yo vā na devaḥ śaśikhaṇḍamauliḥ // DhDaś_2.67 //
children.translated_text: or who is not the God whose crest is the crescent moon (<s>Śiva</s>). (DhDaś 2.67)
Chapter 3
Because it is the archetype of the others, because it embraces more <s>rasas</s>,
and because it possesses the complete [set of] characteristics — the <s>Nāṭaka</s> (drama proper) is described first. (DhDaś 3.1)
Having first performed the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> (preliminary rites), when the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager) has exited,
another actor, entering in the same manner, should introduce the poem [i.e., the play]. (DhDaś 3.2)
He [the <s>sūtradhāra</s>], divine, mortal, or of that [combined] nature — or mixed, being one of the two —

children.text: sūcayed vastu bījaṃ vā mukhaṃ pātramathāpi vā // DhDaś_3.3 //
children.translated_text: should indicate the subject-matter, the seed, the opening, or also the character. (DhDaś 3.3)
Having pleased the audience with sweet verses indicative of the poem's meaning,
taking up some season [as a topic], he should resort to the <s>Bhāratī</s> style. (DhDaś 3.4)
<s>Bhāratī</s> is predominantly a verbal activity in Sanskrit, whose basis is the actor.
Its divisions are: <s>Prarocanā</s>, together with <s>Vīthī</s> and <s>Prahasana</s> [introductory forms]. (DhDaś 3.5)
Therein, <s>Prarocanā</s> is the creation of eager anticipation through praise.
<s>Vīthī</s> and <s>Prahasana</s> too will be described in their own context.
[But] the limbs of <s>Vīthī</s>, being also limbs of the <s>āmukha</s> (introduction), are stated here itself. (DhDaś 3.6)

children.text: sūtradhāro naṭīṃ brūte mārṣaṃ vātha vidūṣakam /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> speaks to the <s>naṭī</s> (actress), or to the '<s>Mārṣa</s>' [colleague], or to the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester).

children.text: svakāryaṃ prastutākṣepi citroktyā yat tadāmukham // DhDaś_3.7 //
children.translated_text: That which [involves] a witty speech touching upon one's own business while bearing on the present [play] — that is the <s>āmukha</s> (prologue). (DhDaś 3.7)

children.text: prastāvanā vā tatra syuḥ kathādghātaḥ pravṛttakam /
children.translated_text: Or there may be a <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) — [its varieties are:] <s>kathodghāta</s>, <s>pravṛttaka</s>,
and <s>prayogātiśaya</s>. And [for] the <s>Vīthī</s>, thirteen limbs [are enumerated]. (DhDaś 3.8)
Where a character enters having taken up a sentence or a meaning equal to what the <s>sūtradhāra</s> [said] —

children.text: gṛhītvā praviśet pātraṃ kathodghāto dvidhaiva saḥ // DhDaś_3.9 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>kathodghāta</s> (sudden introduction of the story), and it is of two kinds. (DhDaś 3.9)
<s>Pravṛttaka</s> (continuation) is an entry brought about by temporal coincidence.
Where, from the indication 'here is this one,' through the device of the <s>sūtradhāra</s>,
a character enters — this is considered <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (theatrical surprise). (DhDaś 3.10)
<s>Udghātyaka</s>, <s>Avalagita</s>, <s>Prapañca</s>, <s>Trigata</s>, <s>Chala</s>,
<s>Vākkelī</s>, <s>Adhivala</s>, <s>Gaṇḍa</s>, <s>Avasyandita</s>, <s>Nālikā</s>,
<s>Asatpralāpa</s>, <s>Vyāhāra</s>, and <s>Mṛdava</s> — [these are] the thirteen [limbs of <s>Vīthī</s>]. (DhDaś 3.11)
Where there is mutual conversation [consisting of] a sequence of words with hidden meaning, or of question and answer,
that is called <s>Udghātyaka</s> (the unlocking), and it is of two kinds. (DhDaś 3.12)
Where, through the convergence in one place [of two different meanings], another purpose is accomplished —

children.text: prastute'nyatra vānyat syāt ta(?) cāvalagitaṃ dvidhā // DhDaś_3.13 //
children.translated_text: or where, while one thing is the subject, another [meaning arises] — that is <s>Avalagita</s> (the ambiguous), [and it is] of two kinds. (DhDaś 3.13)
<s>Prapañca</s> (elaborate banter) is considered mutual false praise, producing humor.
<s>Trigata</s> (the triple) here is the combination of multiple meanings through similarity of sound;
it is held to be the three-way conversation of actors etc. in the <s>pūrvaraṅga</s> (prelim). (DhDaś 3.14)
<s>Chala</s> (deception) is the enticement through pleasant or unpleasant words, [followed by] trickery;

children.text: vinivṛttyāsya vākkelī dvistriḥ pratyuktito'pi vā // DhDaś_3.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vākkelī</s> (verbal play) is a retort given two or three times. (DhDaś 3.15)
<s>Adhivala</s> (outbidding) is speech surpassing the other's speech, through rivalry.
<s>Gaṇḍa</s> (the bolt) is something suddenly uttered with a different meaning yet connected to the present [topic]. (DhDaś 3.16)
Where there is an interpretation of what was said in a different sense — that indeed is <s>Avasyandita</s> (deflection).
<s>Nālikā</s> is exactly like a riddle (<s>prahelikā</s>) — with mockery, having a hidden meaning. (DhDaś 3.17)
<s>Asatpralāpa</s> (incoherent speech) is mostly disconnected talk, [spoken] in response to whatever.
<s>Vyāhāra</s> (utterance) is speech with a different meaning, producing humor and dance.

children.text: doṣā guṇā guṇā doṣā yatra syurmṛdavaṃ hi tat // DhDaś_3.18 //
children.translated_text: Where faults [appear as] virtues and virtues [as] faults — that indeed is <s>Mṛdava</s> (the soft). (DhDaś 3.18)
Having introduced the subject-matter and character by one of these [devices], the <s>sūtradhāra</s>

children.text: prastāvanānte nirgacchet tato vastu prapañcayet // DhDaś_3.19 //
children.translated_text: should exit at the end of the <s>prastāvanā</s>; then [another actor] should develop the plot. (DhDaś 3.19)
Endowed with virtues that are approachable, of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-and-steadfast) type, valorous,
desirous of fame, of great energy — a king who is the protector of the three (<s>Vedas</s>, or the three worlds). (DhDaś 3.20)
Where the hero is of a famous lineage, a royal sage, or divine —
the story, which should be well-known, is to be fashioned as the main [plot] here. (DhDaś 3.21)

children.text: yat tatrānucitaṃ kiñcin nāyakasya rasasya vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever therein is improper for the hero or for the <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: viruddhaṃ tat parityājyamanyathā vā prakalpayet // DhDaś_3.22 //
children.translated_text: [or] contradictory — that should be abandoned, or else devised differently. (DhDaś 3.22)

children.text: ādyantamevaṃ niścitya pañcadhā tad vibhajya ca /
children.translated_text: Having thus determined [the plot] from beginning to end, and having divided it into five [junctures],
one should further divide the portions called <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) into sections (<s>khaṇḍas</s>). (DhDaś 3.23)
Those limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) should be sixty-four — and [there is] also another [element]:
the <s>patākā</s> (sub-plot) and its episode may be fewer [in limbs], with one or more <s>anusandhis</s> (connecting links).
Here, limbs are placed as available; without a [full] juncture, one may place a <s>prakarī</s> (minor episode). (DhDaś 3.24)
At the beginning, one should create a <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (introductory scene) or an <s>aṅka</s> (act), according to the logic of the plot.
Having abandoned what is expected [but] uninteresting, [and avoiding] flavorless expansion of the plot —

children.text: yadā sandarśayet śeṣaṃ kuryād viṣkambhakaṃ tadā // DhDaś_3.25 //
children.translated_text: When one wishes to show the remainder, one should employ a <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude). // DhDaś_3.25 //

children.text: yadā tu sarasaṃ vastu mūlādeva pravartate /
children.translated_text: But when a lively subject-matter proceeds from its very beginning,
then the act should come at the very start, based on the opening or the indication. // DhDaś_3.26 //
The action of the hero being directly visible [to the audience], preceded by the extension of the <s>bindu</s> (drop/germ),
an act (<s>aṅka</s>) is the vehicle of <s>rasa</s>, arranged with subject-matter of various kinds. // DhDaś_3.27 //
Through <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent emotions) and <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), through the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion), and through the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions) —
which are taken up and released — one should accomplish the nourishment of the principal [<s>rasa</s>]. // DhDaś_3.28 //

children.text: na cātirasato vastu dūraṃ vicchinnatāṃ nayet /
children.translated_text: Nor should one lead the subject-matter far from the [principal] <s>rasa</s>, producing discontinuity;

children.text: rasaṃ vā na tirodadhyād vastvalaṅkāralakṣaṇaiḥ // DhDaś_3.29 //
children.translated_text: nor should one obscure the <s>rasa</s> with the subject-matter or the characteristics of ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). // DhDaś_3.29 //

children.text: eko raso'ṅgīkartavyo vīraḥ śṛṅgāra eva vā /
children.translated_text: One <s>rasa</s> should be made the principal — either the <s>vīra</s> (heroic) or the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic);

children.text: aṅgamanye rasāḥ sarve kuryān nirvahaṇe'dbhutam // DhDaś_3.30 //
children.translated_text: all other <s>rasas</s> are subordinate. In the conclusion, one should produce the <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous). // DhDaś_3.30 //
Long journeys, killing, battle, the overthrow of kingdoms and countries,

children.text: saṃrodhaṃ bhojanaṃ snānaṃ surataṃ cānulepanam // DhDaś_3.31 //
children.translated_text: confinement, eating, bathing, love-making, and anointing, // DhDaś_3.31 //
the donning of garments and the like — these should not be shown directly on stage.

children.text: nādhikārivadhaṃ kvāpi tyājyamāvaśyakaṃ na ca // DhDaś_3.32 //
children.translated_text: The killing of the antagonist should never be [depicted] anywhere; and what is indispensable should not be omitted. // DhDaś_3.32 //
An act should depict the action of a single day, concerning a single purpose, with the hero in proximity,
with three or four characters; at the end of an act comes the exit (<s>nirgama</s>). // DhDaś_3.33 //
The <s>patākāsthānakas</s> (flag-stations) are used here; the <s>bindu</s> at the end, like the seed.
Thus the acts should be composed, preceded by the entrance (<s>praveśa</s>) and so forth.
The minimum for a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) is five acts; the maximum is ten. // DhDaś_3.34 //
Now, in the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (social drama), the plot should be invented, based on everyday life;
one should make as the hero one among ministers, <s>Brahmins</s>, or merchants. // DhDaś_3.35 //
He should be <s>dhīrapraśānta</s> (calm and composed), with downfalls, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>;
the rest — <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), <s>praveśakas</s> (introductory scenes), <s>rasas</s>, and so on — should be as in the <s>nāṭaka</s>. // DhDaś_3.36 //

children.text: nāyikā tu dvidhā netuḥ kulastrī gaṇikā tathā /
children.translated_text: The heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) is of two kinds: a woman of good family (<s>kulastrī</s>) and a courtesan (<s>gaṇikā</s>);

children.text: kvacidekaiva kulajā kvāpi dvayaṃ kvacit // DhDaś_3.37 //
children.translated_text: sometimes only a woman of good family alone, sometimes both, sometimes [just one]. // DhDaś_3.37 //
The woman of good family is the inner [heroine], the courtesan is the outer; there is no transgression of these [roles].

children.text: ābhiḥ prakaraṇaṃ tredhā saṅkīrṇaṃ dhūrtasaṅkulam // DhDaś_3.38 //
children.translated_text: By these [combinations], the <s>prakaraṇa</s> is of three kinds: mixed (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) and filled with rogues (<s>dhūrta</s>). // DhDaś_3.38 //
The <s>nāṭikā</s> (minor drama) is also found here, [distinct from] the mixed types, for their avoidance.

children.text: tatra vastu prakaraṇān nāṭakān nāyako nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: In it, the plot comes from the <s>prakaraṇa</s>; from the <s>nāṭaka</s>, the hero is a king,
of well-known [lineage], <s>dhīralalita</s> (gentle and refined); the principal <s>rasa</s> is <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, with its [appropriate] characteristics. // DhDaś_3.39 //
If one wishes to distinguish it by having predominantly female characters, four acts, and so on —
by the difference of one, two, or three acts, characters, and so on, there is endless variety. // DhDaś_3.40 //

children.text: devī tatra bhavej jyeṣṭhā pragalbhā nṛpavaṃśajā /
children.translated_text: The queen (<s>devī</s>) there should be the chief wife, bold, born of a royal lineage,

children.text: gambhīrā māninī kṛcchāt tadvaśān netṛsaṅgamaḥ // DhDaś_3.41 //
children.translated_text: dignified, proud; only with difficulty, through [the queen's] power, does the hero unite [with the other heroine]. // DhDaś_3.41 //
The heroine should be of such a type — naive (<s>mugdhā</s>), divine, and exceedingly charming,
brought near through connection with the harem, etc., and through reports and sightings. // DhDaś_3.42 //
The hero's love for her progresses through nine new stages, one after another.
The hero should proceed there apprehensively, afraid of the queen.
The <s>nāṭikā</s> has <s>kaiśikī</s> (graceful) limbs and four acts arranged [accordingly]. // DhDaś_3.43 //
The <s>bhāṇa</s> (monologue), however, is a rogue's adventures — experienced by oneself or by another —
in which one clever, learned <s>viṭa</s> (libertine) narrates [them]. // DhDaś_3.44 //
He should make addresses, statements, and replies by means of characters spoken to in the air (<s>ākāśabhāṣita</s>);
he should suggest the <s>vīra</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [<s>rasas</s>] through praises of valor and good fortune. // DhDaś_3.45 //
The <s>bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style) should predominate; a single act; the plot is invented;

children.text: mukhanirvahaṇe sāṅge lāsyāṅgāni daśāpi ca // DhDaś_3.46 //
children.translated_text: it has the opening (<s>mukha</s>) and conclusion (<s>nirvahaṇa</s>) as its limbs, and also the ten <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (lyrical components). // DhDaś_3.46 //
<s>Geyapada</s> (song), <s>sthitapāthya</s> (standing recitation), <s>āsīna</s> (seated [recitation]), <s>puṣpagaṇḍikā</s> (flower-cheek),
<s>pracchedaka</s> (cutting piece), <s>trigūḍha</s> (triply concealed), <s>saindhava</s> (the Saindhava), <s>dvigūḍhaka</s> (doubly concealed), // DhDaś_3.47 //
<s>uttamottamaka</s> (the most excellent), and <s>uktapratyukta</s> (statement and response) —
these are the ten-fold classification of lyrical components (<s>lāsyāṅgas</s>) prescribed for an act. // DhDaś_3.48 //
Likewise, the <s>prahasana</s> (farce) is of three kinds: pure (<s>śuddha</s>), distorted (<s>vaikṛta</s>), and mixed (<s>saṅkara</s>).
It is filled with heretics, <s>Brahmins</s>, and the like, or servants, female attendants, and <s>viṭas</s> (libertines);
the action involves stuttering speech; the pure type is accompanied by humorous dialogue. // DhDaś_3.49 //
The distorted type features the speech and dress of lovers and such — eunuchs, disguised doorkeepers, [false] ascetics;
the mixed type, from [the combination of both], is like the <s>vīthī</s> (street-play), filled with rogues.

children.text: rasastu bhūyasā kāryaḥ ṣaḍvidho hāsya eva tu // DhDaś_3.50 //
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s>, for the most part, should be of the six kinds of <s>hāsya</s> (comic) alone. // DhDaś_3.50 //

children.text: ḍime vastu prasiddhaṃ syād vṛttayaḥ kaiśikīṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>ḍima</s> (spectacle play), the plot should be well-known; the styles (<s>vṛttis</s>) exclude the <s>kaiśikī</s>;
the heroes are gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, great <s>nāgas</s>,
<s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and the like — sixteen, all extremely turbulent. // DhDaś_3.51 //
It is accompanied by six intense <s>rasas</s> excluding <s>hāsya</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s>,
with actions involving magic, conjuring, battle, fury, and agitation; // DhDaś_3.52 //
and with eclipses of the sun and moon; when the <s>raudra</s> (furious) <s>rasa</s> is the principal,
the <s>ḍima</s> is recognized as having four acts, four <s>sandhis</s>, and no deliberation (<s>vimarśa</s>). // DhDaś_3.53 //
The <s>vyāyoga</s> (military spectacle) has a well-known plot; it depends on well-known, turbulent men;

children.text: hīno garbhavimarśābhyāṃ dīptāḥ syurḍimavad rasāḥ // DhDaś_3.54 //
children.translated_text: it lacks the <s>garbha</s> (development) and <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation); the <s>rasas</s> should be intense, as in the <s>ḍima</s>. // DhDaś_3.54 //
The battle is not caused by a woman — as in the victory of <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>);
the <s>vyāyoga</s> depicts the action of a single day, in a single act, with many men. // DhDaś_3.55 //
In the <s>samavakāra</s> (ensemble play) too, the opening should be made as in the <s>nāṭaka</s> and such;

children.text: khyātaṃ devāsuraṃ vastu nirvimarśāstu sandhayaḥ // DhDaś_3.56 //
children.translated_text: the plot is well-known, concerning gods and demons; the <s>sandhis</s> are without deliberation. // DhDaś_3.56 //
The styles have subdued <s>kaiśikī</s>; the heroes are gods and demons,

children.text: dvādaśodāttavikhyātāḥ phalaṃ teṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak // DhDaś_3.57 //
children.translated_text: twelve in number, exalted and famous; their outcomes are separate and distinct. // DhDaś_3.57 //
All abound in the <s>vīra</s> <s>rasa</s> — as in the churning of the ocean;
with three acts, three deceptions, three instances of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, three dispersals. // DhDaś_3.58 //
The first act should be made with two <s>sandhis</s> and of twelve <s>nāḍikās</s> (time-units);
the last two are of four and two <s>nāḍikās</s> respectively; a <s>nāḍikā</s> equals two <s>ghaṭikās</s>. // DhDaś_3.59 //
The three deceptions should arise from the nature of the plot, from fate, or from contrivance;
the dispersals are caused by siege of the city, battle, wind, fire, and such. // DhDaś_3.60 //
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is [motivated] by <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>; there is no <s>bindu</s> or <s>praveśaka</s> here.

children.text: vīthyaṅgāni yathālābhaṃ kuryāt prahasane yathā // DhDaś_3.61 //
children.translated_text: One should employ <s>vīthī</s> components as available, as in the <s>prahasana</s>. // DhDaś_3.61 //
The <s>vīthī</s> (street-play) has the <s>kaiśikī</s> style; its <s>sandhis</s>, limbs, and acts are like the <s>bhāṇa</s>;

children.text: rasaḥ sūcyastu śṛṅgāraḥ spṛśedapi rasāntaram // DhDaś_3.62 //
children.translated_text: the <s>rasa</s> to be suggested is <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, though it may touch upon other <s>rasas</s> as well. // DhDaś_3.62 //
It is equipped with <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) and the well-known limbs such as the <s>udghātyaka</s> and others;
thus the <s>vīthī</s> should be composed, employing one or two characters. // DhDaś_3.63 //
In the <s>utsṛṣṭikāṅka</s> (improvised act), one should elaborate a well-known plot with ingenuity;

children.text: rasastu karuṇaḥ sthāyī netāraḥ prākṛtā narāḥ // DhDaś_3.64 //
children.translated_text: the permanent <s>rasa</s> is <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic); the heroes are ordinary men. // DhDaś_3.64 //
Like the <s>bhāṇa</s>, it is equipped with <s>sandhis</s>, styles, and limbs, with women's lamentations;

children.text: vācā yuddhaṃ vidhātavyaṃ tathā jayaparājayau // DhDaś_3.65 //
children.translated_text: battle should be conveyed through speech, as should victory and defeat. // DhDaś_3.65 //
In the <s>ihāmṛga</s> (mixed play), the plot has four acts and three <s>sandhis</s>;
the hero and antagonist follow human, divine, and earthly norms. // DhDaś_3.66 //
Both are well-known and <s>dhīroddhata</s> (bold and haughty); the final [reversal] makes an inappropriate action through reversal.
The hero abducts a divine woman against her will, and the antagonist does not desire [the outcome]. // DhDaś_3.67 //
One should show just a little semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in this [type];
having brought the conflict to its peak, one should avert the battle by a stratagem.

children.text: vadhaprāptasya kurvīta vadhaṃ naiva mahātmanaḥ // DhDaś_3.68 //
children.translated_text: One should never depict the killing of a great soul who has come to the point of death. // DhDaś_3.68 //
Thus, having reflected upon the path of the ten dramatic forms and their characteristics,
having examined the subject-matter and contemplated the compositions of poets,
one should compose a work, adorned effortlessly with ornaments,
with words noble and sweet, in meters clear and gentle. // DhDaś_3.69 //
Chapter 4
Through <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent emotions), <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary psycho-physical reactions), and <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotions),

children.text: ānīyamānaḥ svādyatvaṃ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ // DhDaś_4.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion), being brought to a state of relish-ability, is called <s>rasa</s>. // DhDaś_4.1 //
Among these, the <s>vibhāva</s> nourishes the emotion by making it known;
it is twofold in division: <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). // DhDaś_4.2 //
The <s>anubhāva</s> is the modification that indicates the emotion.
The establishment of cause and effect between them is through conventional usage. // DhDaś_4.3 //
The bringing about of one emotion by other emotions such as happiness, sorrow, and the like is called the nourishment of that emotion.
Other emotions that are distinct, even while serving as <s>anubhāvas</s>, are <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary);
because they arise from <s>sattva</s> (the heart/being) alone — and that too is the nourishment of that emotion. // DhDaś_4.4 //
<s>Stambha</s> (stupor), <s>pralaya</s> (fainting), <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation), <s>sveda</s> (perspiration), <s>vaivarṇya</s> (discoloration), <s>vepathu</s> (trembling),
<s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>vaisvārya</s> (change of voice) — these are the eight [<s>sāttvika bhāvas</s>]. <s>Stambha</s> here is the state of the body being without action;
<s>pralaya</s> is the loss of consciousness; the rest have well-known characteristics. // DhDaś_4.5 //
Moving especially in the direction [of the permanent emotion], the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions)
emerge from and submerge into the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion), like waves in the ocean. // DhDaś_4.6 //

<s>Nirveda</s> (world-weariness), <s>glāni</s> (debility), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>śrama</s> (exhaustion), <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupidity), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>dainya</s> (despondency), <s>augrya</s> (ferocity), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety) —
Terror, jealousy, intolerance, pride, recollection, death, intoxication, sleep, drowsiness, awakening,
shame, epileptic seizure, delusion, discernment, indolence, agitation, deliberation, dissimulation,
sickness, madness, despair, eagerness, and restlessness — these are the thirty-three [transitory states]. (DhDaś 4.7)
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency) [arises] from knowledge of truth, calamity, jealousy, and the like — it is self-deprecation.
Therein [the indicators are]: anxiety, tears, sighing, pallor, gasping, and dejection. (DhDaś 4.8)
<s>Glāni</s> (weakness) [arises] from love and the like, exhaustion, thirst, and hunger — it is lifelessness; herein
[the indicators are]: pallor, trembling, lack of enthusiasm, emaciation of limbs, and [weakness of] speech and action. (DhDaś 4.9)
<s>Śaṅkā</s> (apprehension) is the premonition of misfortune, [arising] from the cruelty of others or one's own misconduct;
herein [the indicators are]: trembling, drying [of the throat], anxious glancing about, and change of complexion and voice. (DhDaś 4.10)
<s>Śrama</s> (fatigue) is weariness from travel, lovemaking, and the like; herein [the indicators are] perspiration, rubbing [of limbs], and the like.
<s>Dhṛti</s> (contentment) [arises] from knowledge, power, and the like — it produces undisturbed enjoyment. (DhDaś 4.11)
<s>Apratipatti</s> (bewilderment) is mental paralysis (<s>jaḍatā</s>), occurring from seeing or hearing what is desired or undesired;
therein [the indicators are]: unblinking gaze, staring, silence, and the like. (DhDaś 4.12)
<s>Prasatti</s> (delight) [arises] from festivals and the like; <s>harṣa</s> (joy) — [its indicators are] tears, perspiration, and stammering.
<s>Dainya</s> (wretchedness) [arises] from poverty and the like — lack of spirit, [indicated by] dark complexion, weeping, and the like. (DhDaś 4.13)
<s>Caṇḍatā</s> (fierceness) [arises] when offended — from transgression, hostility, and cruelty; [it is] severity.
Therein [the indicators are]: perspiration, head-shaking, threatening, striking, and the like. (DhDaś 4.14)
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is thought [arising] from non-attainment of what is desired; it produces emptiness, sighing, and burning.
<s>Trāsa</s> (terror) [arises] from thunder and the like — agitation of the mind; herein [the indicators are] trembling and the like. (DhDaś 4.15)
<s>Asūyā</s> (envy) is the inability to bear another's excellence — born of pride, ill-nature, and anger;
[its indicators are]: fault-finding, contempt, frowning, and gestures of anger and ire. (DhDaś 4.16)
<s>Amarṣa</s> (intolerance) [arises] from abuse and insult — it is a fierce determination;
therein [the indicators are]: distress, head-shaking, threatening, striking, and the like. (DhDaś 4.17)
<s>Garva</s> (pride) is intoxication (<s>mada</s>) arising from noble birth, beauty, strength, sovereignty, and the like;
its actions are: arrogance, contempt, and a coquettish self-survey of one's limbs. (DhDaś 4.18)
<s>Smṛti</s> (recollection) [arises] from cognition of similar things, thought, and the like, through latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>); herein also
in cognition that reveals an object as already known, [the indicators are]: raising of the brow, and the like.
Death (<s>maraṇa</s>) is not [separately] described because it is well known and because it is an unfavorable [outcome for drama]. (DhDaś 4.19)
<s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is elation of joy, from drinking — [indicated by] stumbling limbs, speech, and gait;
<s>Nidrā</s> (sleep), laughter, and also weeping occur therein, in superior, middle, and inferior [types of intoxication respectively].

children.text: suptaṃ nidrodbhavaṃ tatra śvāsocchāsakriyā param // DhDaś_4.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Supta</s> (the state of being asleep) arises from sleep; therein [the indicators are] breathing, exhalation, and involuntary action. (DhDaś 4.20)
<s>Nidrā</s> (drowsiness) is the closing of the mind, [arising] from worry, laziness, fatigue, and the like;
therein [the indicators are]: yawning, stretching, closing of the eyes, dreaming, and the like.
<s>Vibodha</s> (awakening) [arises] from the completion [of sleep] and the like; therein [the indicators are] yawning and rubbing of the eyes. (DhDaś 4.21)
<s>Vrīḍā</s> (shame) [arises] from misconduct and the like — it is the absence of boldness; one should represent it
through turning the body aside, covering [the face], pallor, looking downward, and the like. (DhDaś 4.22)
<s>Apasmāra</s> (epileptic seizure) [arises] from possession, suffering, and the like — an attack according to its type;
[its indicators are]: falling to the ground, trembling, frothing at the mouth, foam rising, and the like. (DhDaś 4.23)
<s>Moha</s> (delusion) is a distraction of mind [arising] from fear, suffering, possession, and excessive thought;
therein [the indicators are]: ignorance, confusion, reeling, dizziness, and failure to perceive. (DhDaś 4.24)
<s>Mati</s> (discernment) is the knowledge of truth, [arising] from the removal of error or from instruction in the <s>śāstras</s> and the like.
<s>Ālasya</s> (indolence) [arises] from fatigue, pregnancy, and the like — [indicated by] yawning, sighing, and the like. (DhDaś 4.25)
<s>Āvega</s> (agitation) [arises from various causes]: in battle, [it manifests as] an attack with weapons and elephants;
from wind, the body is covered with dust, with hurried steps; from rain, the limbs are huddled together;
from a portent, the limbs collapse; [depending on] whether it causes harm or benefit, the effects are of grief or joy;
from fire, the face is confused with smoke; from an elephant, [one experiences] both [types of] fear — with paralysis, trembling, and flight. (DhDaś 4.26)
<s>Tarka</s> (deliberation) is reasoning about a doubt — [indicated by] dancing of the brows, head, and fingers.
<s>Avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) is the concealment of one's transformation due to shame and the like — [indicated by] altered body [movements].
Diseases (<s>vyādhi</s>) [arise] from disorders of the humors (<s>sannipāta</s>) and the like — their details are found elsewhere. (DhDaś 4.27)
<s>Unmāda</s> (madness) is acting without regard [to propriety], [arising] from disorders of the humors, possession, and the like;
herein [the indicators according to different] states are: weeping, singing, laughter, sighing, and the like. (DhDaś 4.28)
<s>Viṣāda</s> (despair) [arises] from the failure to accomplish an undertaken task — it is the collapse of courage;
[it is] characterized by sighing, gasping, burning of the heart, and seeking companions. (DhDaś 4.29)
<s>Autsukyam</s> (eagerness) is the inability to bear the passage of time, [arising] from desire for pleasures, love, and battle;
therein [the indicators are]: gasping, sighing, burning of the heart, perspiration, and agitation. (DhDaś 4.30)
<s>Cāpala</s> (restlessness) is instability, [arising] from jealousy, hatred, passion, and the like;
therein [the indicators are]: reproaching, harshness, willful conduct, and the like. (DhDaś 4.31)
The <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent state) is interrupted by [other] states, whether opposed or unopposed;

children.text: ātmabhāvaṃ nayatyanyān sa sthāyī lavaṇākaraḥ // DhDaś_4.32 //
children.translated_text: [yet] it brings [them] under its own nature — that permanent state is [like] the ocean [absorbing rivers]. (DhDaś 4.32)

children.text: ratyutsāhajgupsāḥ krodho hāsaḥ smayo bhayaṃ śokaḥ /
children.translated_text: Love (<s>rati</s>), heroic ardor (<s>utsāha</s>), revulsion (<s>jugupsā</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), laughter (<s>hāsa</s>), wonder (<s>smaya</s>), fear (<s>bhaya</s>), and grief (<s>śoka</s>) —

children.text: śamamapi kecit prāhuḥ puṣṭirnāṭyeṣu naitasya // DhDaś_4.33 //
children.translated_text: some declare tranquility (<s>śama</s>) as well, [but] its nourishment is not [demonstrated] in dramas. (DhDaś 4.33)
How can detachment (<s>nirveda</s>) and the like be relished as a permanent state, since [they are merely] attendant upon love and the rest?
They lead only to distaste [not <s>rasa</s>] — therefore eight are considered the permanent states. (DhDaś 4.34)

children.text: vācyā prakaraṇādibhyo buddhisthā vā yathā kriyā /
children.translated_text: Whether expressed through dialogue, context, and the like, or residing in the intellect — as is the action,
so is the sentence-meaning connected with agents (<s>kāraka</s>); the permanent state [relates to] <s>bhāvas</s> and the others likewise. (DhDaś 4.35)

children.text: rasaḥ sa eva svādvyatvād rasikasyaiva vartanāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is that very [permanent state], because of [its] savor-like [quality]; because it exists only for the connoisseur (<s>rasika</s>);
because the actor does not [truly] experience it; and because poetry is not directed exclusively toward that [literal experience]. (DhDaś 4.36)
The experience (<s>pratīti</s>) of the spectator — through contact with shame, jealousy, passion, and hatred —
is like viewing a worldly person who is united with his own beloved. (DhDaś 4.37)
The <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble hero) and the rest, being conditions [for rasa], are illustrated by <s>Rāma</s> and others;

children.text: vibhāvayati ratyādīn svadante rasikasya te // DhDaś_4.38 //
children.translated_text: they give rise to love and the rest — and these are relished by the connoisseur. (DhDaś 4.38)
Just as children, playing with clay elephants and the like,
relish their own enthusiasm — so too do the audience [relish theirs] through [characters like] <s>Arjuna</s> and the rest. (DhDaś 4.39)
The actor's relishing of the meaning of poetry through imaginative realization (<s>bhāvanā</s>) cannot be prevented;
[but] his relish arises from identification with the meaning of the poem — [it is] born from inner bliss. (DhDaś 4.40)
That [rasa] is fourfold — through expansion, diffusion, agitation, and transport —
in the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), heroic (<s>vīra</s>), disgusting (<s>bībhatsa</s>), and furious (<s>raudra</s>) [rasas respectively], in the mind, in order. (DhDaś 4.41)
Those same [modifications belong] to the comic (<s>hāsya</s>), marvelous (<s>adbhuta</s>), terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s>), and pathetic (<s>karuṇa</s>) [rasas];
hence their derivation from those [former four], and hence the ascertainment [that they are derivative]. (DhDaś 4.42)
The excellence of tranquility (<s>śama</s>) is not to be [separately] described; joy (<s>muditā</s>) and the like constitute its nature;
its elements — the moon, detachment, horripilation, and the like — being its characteristic forms,
having attained from the poem the semblance of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory states), and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) — (DhDaś 4.43)

children.text: bhāvitaḥ svadate sthāyī rasaḥ sa parikīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: the permanent state, being thus nourished, is relished — that is declared to be <s>rasa</s>.
There is identity of definition due to identity of the <s>vibhāvas</s> — hence non-difference between <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>. (DhDaś 4.44)
Through enjoyment of beautiful places, seasons, times, attire, pleasures, and the like,
<s>rati</s> (love), whose essence is delight, is that very [feeling] between a young man and woman mutually enamored;
when it blossoms, it becomes <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic rasa), through sweet bodily gestures. (DhDaś 4.45)

children.text:
ye sattvajāḥ sthāyin eva cāṣṭau
triṃśat trayo ye vyabhicāriṇaśca /

children.translated_text: and the thirty-three transitory states —
these forty-nine emotions (<s>bhāvas</s>), when skillfully bound together, nourish [<s>rasa</s>].
Sloth, fierceness, death, and revulsion —
[when associated with] its substrate — are considered incompatible with the duality [of love in union]. (DhDaś 4.46)
The eight [permanent states] that are born of character (<s>sattva</s>), the very eight permanent states,
Therein, non-union (<s>ayoga</s>) [occurs] even in mutual love, between two young people of one mind;
separation (<s>asaṅgama</s>) [arises] from dependence [on others], from fate, or from physical distance. (DhDaś 4.47)
That [love-in-separation] has ten stages. Therein, first is longing (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), then brooding (<s>cintana</s>),
recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), recounting of virtues (<s>guṇakathā</s>), agitation (<s>udvega</s>), raving (<s>pralāpa</s>), madness (<s>unmāda</s>), fever (<s>sañjvara</s>),

children.text: jaḍatā maraṇaṃ ceti duravasthaṃ yathottaram // DhDaś_4.48 //
children.translated_text: stupor (<s>jaḍatā</s>), and death (<s>maraṇa</s>) — each progressively more severe. (DhDaś 4.48)
<s>Abhilāṣa</s> (longing) is the desire therein for the beloved, who is beautiful in every limb,

children.text: dṛṣṭe śrute vā tatrāpi vismayānandasādhvasāḥ // DhDaś_4.49 //
children.translated_text: whether seen or heard of; therein [arise] wonder, bliss, and trepidation. (DhDaś 4.49)
Seeing [occurs] directly, in a portrait, in a dream, in a reflection, or in an illusion;
hearing [occurs] indirectly — through the song of a companion, the praise of a bard, and the like, extolling virtues. (DhDaś 4.50)
The [states] with <s>anubhāvas</s> and <s>vibhāvas</s> — brooding and the rest — have been previously shown.
The tenfold staging has been mostly illustrated by the preceptors through their styles (<s>vṛtti</s>);
in the compositions of great poets, their infiniteness is observed. (DhDaś 4.51)

children.text: dṛṣṭe śrute'bhilāṣāc ca kiṃ nautsukyaṃ prajāyate /
children.translated_text: Upon seeing or hearing, from longing — does not eagerness (<s>autsukyam</s>) arise?

children.text: aprāptau kiṃ na nirvedo glāniḥ kiṃ nāticintanāt // DhDaś_4.52 //
children.translated_text: In non-attainment, does not despondency (<s>nirveda</s>) arise? Does not weakness (<s>glāni</s>) arise from excessive brooding? (DhDaś 4.52)
<s>Viprayoga</s> (separation) is parting — twofold: between those with established intimacy (<s>vibhrama</s>).

Through the distinction of love-quarrel (<s>māna</s>) and [physical] absence (<s>pravāsa</s>); <s>māna</s> too is of two kinds: from affection (<s>praṇaya</s>) and from jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>). (DhDaś 4.53)
Therein, <s>praṇayamāna</s> (affectionate quarrel) occurs between the two when anger subsides;
the jealousy-born <s>māna</s> of women is anger toward the beloved who associates with another;

children.text: śrute vānumite dṛṣṭe śrutistatra sakhīmukhāt // DhDaś_4.54 //
children.translated_text: whether heard, inferred, or directly seen. Hearing therein [is] through the mouth of a companion. (DhDaś 4.54)
[It is] constructed from dreaming of enjoyment, a slip of the tongue [speaking another's name] while in one's arms;
the inferential type is threefold; the directly-seen is within the range of one's own senses. (DhDaś 4.55)
Each successively more serious, one should address that [māna] through six means:
by conciliation (<s>sāma</s>), by creating a rift (<s>bheda</s>), by gifts (<s>dāna</s>), by bowing down, by strategic neglect, and by introducing another <s>rasa</s>. (DhDaś 4.56)
There, kind words (<s>sāma</s>) are conciliatory speech; <s>bheda</s> (division) is the acquiring of her friend's [alliance];

children.text: dānaṃ vyājena bhūṣādeḥ pādayoḥ patanaṃ natiḥ // DhDaś_4.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>dāna</s> (gift) is [giving] ornaments and such by means of a pretext; prostration is falling at [her] feet. (DhDaś 4.57)
When <s>sāma</s> and the rest are exhausted, there should be <s>upekṣā</s> (indifference) or <s>avadhīraṇa</s> (disregard).
From impetuosity, fear, joy, and the like, the loss of anger [is] <s>rasāntara</s> (transition to another <s>rasa</s>);
and the gestures of anger in women have been described previously. (DhDaś 4.58)
From necessity, from confusion, or from a curse — exile (<s>pravāsa</s>) is the separation of the two [lovers] to different places;
therein: tears, sighs, emaciation, and disheveled locks, and the like. (DhDaś 4.59)
The second [type of separation] arises suddenly, from a divine, human, or [natural] calamity;
born from a curse, which transforms one's own form — even in [the other's] presence. (DhDaś 4.60)

children.text: mṛte tvekatra yatrānyaḥ pralapecchoka eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: When one of the two has died and the other laments — that is <s>śoka</s> (grief) itself;

children.text: vyāśrayatvān na śṛṅgāraḥ pratyāpanne tu netaraḥ // DhDaś_4.61 //
children.translated_text: because of [its] dependence on [a different emotional] basis, it is not <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment); but when [the beloved] returns, it is nothing else [but <s>śṛṅgāra</s>]. (DhDaś 4.61)
The <s>utkā</s> (eager one) is she whose beloved is on a journey due to love-absence; <s>proṣitapriyā</s> is she whose beloved is abroad;
the <s>vipralabdhā</s> (deceived one) is she who is in a quarrel from jealousy; and the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (injured one) is she whose beloved has been with another. (DhDaś 4.62)
Where two lovers serve each other with mutual favor,
[enjoying] seeing, touching, and the like — that is <s>sambhoga</s> (enjoyment in union), accompanied by delight. (DhDaś 4.63)
Therein, the activities that proceed are the ten [types of] <s>līlā</s> (playful gestures) and other [behaviors] of women,
befitting the beloved, [arising] from courtesy, tenderness, and love. (DhDaś 4.64)
The lover should delight her through flattery, through arts, games, and the like;

children.text: na grāmyamācaret kiñcin narmabhraṃśakaraṃ na ca // DhDaś_4.65 //
children.translated_text: he should not perform anything vulgar, nor anything that would destroy the jest. (DhDaś 4.65)
The <s>vīra</s> (heroic) [<s>rasa</s>], whose ground is valor (<s>utsāha</s>), [is accompanied by] prowess, courtesy,
resolve, fortitude, bewilderment, despondency, statecraft, wonder, valor, and the like;
it is threefold — from compassion, from battle, and from generosity;
therein [the attendant states are] intelligence, pride, steadfastness, and great joy. (DhDaś 4.66)
The <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) [<s>rasa</s>], whose sole ground is revulsion (<s>jugupsā</s>), [arises] from worms, putrid smells, vomiting, and the like;
the <s>udvega</s> (agitation) [variety arises] from blood, entrails, hair, bones, and fat and flesh;
the pure (<s>śuddha</s>) [variety arises] from disgust (<s>ghṛṇā</s>) at the buttocks, breasts, and such, due to detachment, and is surrounded by <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent states)
such as contortion of the nose and face; here, [the transitory states are] revulsion, pain, fear, and the like. (DhDaś 4.67)
The <s>raudra</s> (furious) [<s>rasa</s>] is the offspring of anger (<s>krodha</s>), nourished by envy, enmity, and distortion;
agitation, with biting of the lower lip, trembling, knitting of the brows, perspiration, and reddening of the face;
exultation over the enemy, boasting, striking of flesh and ground, vows, and seizure [of weapons] —
herein, intolerance (<s>amarṣa</s>), pride (<s>mada</s>), recollection, restlessness, envy, and fierce impetuosity, and the like. (DhDaś 4.68)
From distorted appearance, speech, or attire — of oneself or of another —

children.text: hāsaḥ syāt paripoṣo'sya hāsyastriprakṛtiḥ smṛtaḥ // DhDaś_4.69 //
children.translated_text: arises laughter (<s>hāsa</s>); its nourishment is <s>hāsya</s> (the comic <s>rasa</s>), remembered as being of three types. (DhDaś 4.69)

children.text: smitamiha vikāsinayanaṃ kiñcillakṣyadvijaṃ tu hasitaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: A <s>smita</s> (smile) here has eyes slightly expanded and barely visible teeth; <s>hasita</s> (gentle laughter) [shows teeth slightly more];
<s>vihasita</s> (open laughter) has a sweet sound; this <s>upahasita</s> (derisive laughter) is accompanied by shaking of the head; (DhDaś 4.70)
<s>apahasita</s> (excessive laughter) has tearful eyes; <s>atihasita</s> (uproarious laughter) has the body thrown about;

children.text: dve dve hasite caiṣāṃ jyeṣṭhe madhye'dhame kramaśaḥ // DhDaś_4.71 //
children.translated_text: of these, two each [belong to] the superior, middle, and inferior [characters] respectively. (DhDaś 4.71)
Drowsiness, lethargy, fatigue, sickness, and fainting are its accompaniments.

children.text: atilokaiḥ padārthaiḥ syād vismayātmā raso'dbhutaḥ // DhDaś_4.72 //
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> whose essence is wonder (<s>vismaya</s>), [arising] from extraordinary objects, is the <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous). (DhDaś 4.72)
Its [outward] manifestations are exclamations of 'well done!', tears, trembling, perspiration, and stammering;
its transitory states (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) are primarily joy, agitation, and steadfastness. (DhDaś 4.73)
From distorted voice, form, and the like, the emotion of fear is the <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible) [<s>rasa</s>],
characterized by trembling of all limbs, perspiration, drying [of the mouth], and bewilderment;
its concomitants are despondency, confusion, delusion, terror, and the like. (DhDaś 4.74)
From the loss of what is desired or the attainment of what is undesired — the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic) [<s>rasa</s>], whose essence is grief (<s>śoka</s>); following it,
sighs, gasping, weeping, stupor, wild lamenting, and the like; (DhDaś 4.75)
fainting, epilepsy, despondency, mental anguish, death-like [state], lethargy, bewilderment,
despair, torpor, madness, anxiety, and so forth are the transitory states (<s>vyabhicārin</s>). (DhDaś 4.76)
Emotions (<s>bhāva</s>) such as love, devotion, and the like, and <s>rasas</s> such as [the pleasure of] hunting, gambling, and the like,
because they are clearly subsumable under joy, valor, and the rest, are not enumerated [separately]. (DhDaś 4.77)
The thirty-six ornaments (<s>bhūṣaṇa</s>) and the like, and the twenty-one [devices] such as <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and the rest,
the objects, junctures, sub-divisions, and internal elements — along with their embellishments (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) — [have been described]. (DhDaś 4.78)
That which is charming, that which is repulsive, that which is lofty, or even that which is lowly,

children.text: ugraṃ prasādi gahanaṃ vikṛtaṃ ca vastu /
children.translated_text: that which is fierce, that which is serene, that which is dense, and that which is bizarre —
whatever [object], whether real or imaginary, is conceived by the poet's creative faculty,

children.text: tan nāsti yan na rasabhāvamupaiti loke // DhDaś_4.79 //
children.translated_text: there is nothing in the world that cannot attain the state of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>. (DhDaś 4.79)
By <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, son of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
the cause of the delight of the minds of the learned,
who partook of the wit of the court of the lord of <s>Muñja</s>,
this <s>Daśarūpaka</s> has been made manifest. (DhDaś 4.80)
